name: Vinod Khosla
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: Forbes' own profile page names Vinod Khosla and states "Vinod Khosla is ranked at No. 1 on the 2026 Midas List, his 19th appearance" (https://www.forbes.com/profile/vinod-khosla/). a1: born 28 January 1955 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinod_Khosla). a2: Stanford MBA 1980, his last completed credential (after IIT Delhi BTech electrical engineering 1976 and a Carnegie Mellon master's); Wikipedia states he "received his MBA in 1980". a3: 1986, "In 1986, Khosla joined the venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins as a general partner" -- his first job in the investing domain (the 1980 Daisy Systems CFO role is a finance title inside an operating company he co-founded, so it is recorded as a4, not a3). a4: 1980, Daisy Systems, where Wikipedia says he "became the first full-time founder and chief financial officer"; Sun Microsystems (1982) is his second venture. SERIAL-FOUNDER / EARLIER-FIRM CALL, EXPLICIT: Khosla is a serial founder (Daisy Systems 1980, Sun Microsystems 1982) but his bucket is investors_finance and the criterion is fund100, so operating ventures cannot supply the hit. The fund-form version of the rule bites instead: he was a NAMED GENERAL PARTNER at Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers from 1986, eighteen years before founding Khosla Ventures in 2004, so the hit must be the first qualifying KPCB fund, NOT a Khosla Ventures fund. Dating this row on Khosla Ventures would have been eighteen-plus years late. No earlier GP role than KPCB 1986 was found. BOUNDED fund100 1986-1992, BOTH ENDS SOURCED. Lower end: he cannot be a named GP of a fund that closed before he became a general partner, and he became one in 1986 (Wikipedia; encyclopedia.com's International Directory of Company Histories entry independently says he "had joined Kleiner Perkins in 1986"). Upper end: "KPCB VI, the firm's sixth fund, raised $173 million in 1992" (https://www.encyclopedia.com/books/politics-and-business-magazines/kleiner-perkins-caufield-byers), closed while Khosla was a KPCB general partner (he stayed until 2004). CONSTANT-DOLLAR CHECK: the 1992 fund100 bar is $43,579,143 nominal (python -m src.cpi 1992). $173,000,000 is 397% of that bar -- margin far above 20%, so the upper end is not close. The 1986 bar is $34,043,293; KPCB's funds were already $150M-scale by 1982, so any KPCB fund closing inside the 1986-1992 window would also clear it, which is why the true answer is probably 1986 or 1987 rather than 1992. WHY NOT PINNED: two genuine attempts (WebSearch on KPCB fund closes 1986-1989 with partner lists; encyclopedia.com/fundinguniverse company history; Wikipedia's Kleiner Perkins article, which gives no per-fund table) failed to produce a source that both dates a KPCB fund close between 1986 and 1991 and names its general partners. Form D was a paper filing before 2008, so SEC EDGAR has nothing from this era. PitchBook's KPCB IV profile (1986 vintage, reportedly $150M) returned HTTP 403 and is not cited. Rather than pin 1986 on an unverified vintage year, the row is bounded 1986-1992 at medium confidence; the midpoint the clocks use is 1989. a6: October 2021, Khosla Ventures "raised $1.4 billion in funding to invest in early-to-late stage startups" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khosla_Ventures) -- the scale marker at his own firm, well after the hit.

name: Eric Vishria
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: WebFetch's rendering of the Forbes profile dropped the rank line, so the page was re-pulled with curl and a browser User-Agent; its meta description reads verbatim "Eric Vishria is #3 on Forbes' 2026 The Midas List: Top Tech Investors list", and the embedded list JSON records Midas ranks of 3 (2026), 23 (2025), 16 (2024), 17 (2023) and 59 (2022) (https://www.forbes.com/profile/eric-vishria/). a1: born 1979 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Vishria); corroborated by the Forbes profile giving his age as 47 in 2026. a2 BOUNDED 1998-1999, LOW CONF: Wikipedia states "Vishria graduated from Stanford University at age 19 with a B.S. in mathematical and computational science" but gives no graduation year. Born 1979 + age 19 places the degree in 1998 or 1999 depending on birthday; recorded as that two-year span rather than pinned or dropped, since a2 is the study's binding anchor. Second attempt (Forbes profile) gives "Bachelor of Science, Stanford University" with no year. a3 BOUNDED 1998-1999, LOW CONF: Wikipedia states "He began his career in investment banking at Broadview International and got his first entrepreneurial experience as an early employee at Loudcloud". Investment banking is the finance domain, so Broadview is a3, not the 2014 Benchmark hire (same treatment as p150 Neil Shen, whose a3 is his Citibank job, not his VC job). The bracket: he cannot have started before graduating (1998 at the earliest, per a2) and he was an early employee at Loudcloud, which was founded in 1999. No source gives the year directly. a4: RockMelt -- "In October 2008, Vishria left HP to co-found RockMelt with Tim Howes" (Wikipedia); the browser launched Nov 2010 and Yahoo acquired it in 2013. SERIAL-FOUNDER / EARLIER-FIRM CALL, EXPLICIT: RockMelt (2008) is an operating venture, and its Yahoo sale was reported at $60-70M -- but the bucket is investors_finance and the criterion is fund100, so an operating exit cannot supply the hit. On the fund-form rule, NO EARLIER GP ROLE EXISTS: he was an operator (Broadview, Loudcloud, Opsware, RockMelt, Yahoo) until Benchmark hired him in July 2014, his first partnership anywhere. FUND100 PINNED 2018, from SEC Form D related-person lists, which are what "named general partner" means here. Benchmark Capital Partners IX, L.P. (CIK 0001754447), Form D filed 1 Oct 2018, total offering $425,000,000, lists "Vishria Eric H. ... Managing Member of the General Partner" (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1754447/000175444718000001/xslFormDX01/primary_doc.xml). The 2018 fund100 bar is $77,997,347 nominal (python -m src.cpi 2018); $425,000,000 is 545% of it. The parallel Benchmark Founders' Fund IX, L.P. also names him and sold $122,700,000 with first sale 1 Oct 2018 -- 157% of the same bar -- so 2018 clears on either vehicle. EARLIER FUNDS CHECKED AND REJECTED, WITH FIGURES. An EDGAR full-text search for "Vishria" across all Form D filings returned 26 hits; the four Benchmark vehicles predating Fund IX are: Benchmark Capital Partners VIII, L.P. ($425M, Form D 6 Dec 2013) -- names Cohler, Fenton, Gurley, Lasky and Spurlock and NOT Vishria, because he did not join until July 2014, so he was not a named GP of it; Benchmark Founders' Fund VIII, L.P. ($66,925,000, first sale 21 Feb 2014, D/A 26 Feb 2015) -- names him, but is only 91.0% of the 2014 bar of $73,533,514; Benchmark Founders' Fund VIII-B, L.P. ($58,175,000, same first-sale date) -- names him, 79.1% of the 2014 bar; and Benchmark Capital Partners VII - Annex, L.P. ($42,500,000, first sale 15 Jan 2016) -- names him, 57.0% of the 2016 bar of $74,549,532. FLAGGED NEAR MISS AND ALTERNATIVE READING: Founders' Fund VIII at 91.0% of the bar is a margin under 20%, and VIII and VIII-B share a first-sale date, a related-person list and an address, so a reader who treats them as two vehicles of one fund program would aggregate them to $125,100,000 (170% of the 2014 bar) and date this row 2014 instead of 2018. That aggregation is NOT recorded here because no source says the two are one fund -- it would be my inference, which the brief forbids -- and because every other fund100 row in this dataset names a single L.P. Recorded so the adversarial re-check can see the alternative rather than rediscover it. a6: UNKNOWN. Benchmark deliberately holds its flagship fund flat at $425M (Fund VIII 2013, Fund IX 2018, Benchmark Partners 1 in 2024 all $425,000,000 per their Form Ds), so no later, larger fund exists to serve as a scale marker; recorded unknown rather than repeating the hit figure.

name: Peter Thiel
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED: Forbes' own profile page, pulled with curl and a browser User-Agent, reads "Peter Thiel returns to the Midas List for a 16th time as the cofounder and general partner of venture fund Founders Fund", and its embedded list JSON records him at rank 5 on The Midas List: Top Tech Investors 2026 (https://www.forbes.com/profile/peter-thiel/). The same sentence is also the source for his being a NAMED general partner of Founders Fund; foundersfund.com/team/peter-thiel/ lists his title simply as "Partner". a1: born 11 October 1967, Frankfurt (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Thiel). a2: Stanford Law School JD, 1992 -- his last completed credential, after a Stanford BA in philosophy in 1989. a3: 1993, derivatives trader at Credit Suisse, his first job in the finance domain (the 1992-93 Edmondson clerkship and the sub-one-year stint at Sullivan & Cromwell are law, not finance). Same treatment as p150 Neil Shen, whose a3 is his banking job rather than his VC job. Conf medium: Wikipedia says he started "in 1993" without a month. a4: 1996, Thiel Capital Management -- "with financial support from friends and family, he raised $1 million" (Wikipedia). That is his first venture of any kind; Confinity/PayPal (1998) is second. SERIAL-FOUNDER / EARLIER-FIRM CALL, EXPLICIT -- THIS IS THE JUDGMENT ON THIS ROW. Thiel is a serial founder (Thiel Capital Management 1996, Confinity/PayPal 1998, Palantir 2003, Founders Fund 2005, Valar 2010, Mithril 2012), but the bucket is investors_finance and the criterion is fund100, so operating ventures cannot supply the hit. Two earlier FUND vehicles were checked. (1) Thiel Capital Management, 1996: $1,000,000 raised, against a 1996 fund100 bar of $48,735,335 -- 2.1% of the bar, nowhere near. (2) CLARIUM CAPITAL, founded 2002 with $10,000,000 of his PayPal proceeds and grown to billions by 2008 -- this is the one that could move the row four or five years earlier, and it is REJECTED FOR TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS. First, on the criterion's plain words: fund100 fires on a FUND CLOSING above the bar, and Clarium was an open-ended macro hedge fund with continuous subscription and redemption (Wikipedia's article discusses client redemptions driving AUM down from $7.8bn in June 2008 to $1.5bn in July 2009), so it has no closing event to date at all. Second, on evidence: after three attempts (the Wikipedia Clarium Capital article, the Wikipedia Peter Thiel article, and a targeted search) NO CITABLE SOURCE gives Clarium's assets under management for any year from 2002 through 2006 -- Wikipedia's earliest AUM figure is $4bn at the start of 2008, and the only 2005 figure surfaced came from an LLM-generated wiki that is not citable here. So even under the more generous reading the crossing year cannot be sourced. FLAGGED for adversarial re-check: if a reviewer holds that a hedge fund's AUM crossing counts as fund100 AND finds a dated pre-2007 Clarium AUM figure in a real source, this row moves earlier. FUND100 PINNED 2007: Founders Fund II, $220,000,000. TechCrunch's report of the close is dated 17 December 2007 and opens "San Francisco based Founders Fund launched in 2005 with a $50 million venture fund" (https://techcrunch.com/?p=12224); Wikipedia's Founders Fund article independently lists Fund II as 2007 / $220 million. The 2007 fund100 bar is $64,403,326 nominal (python -m src.cpi 2007); $220,000,000 is 342% of it. FLAGGED NEAR MISS, MARGIN UNDER 20%: Founders Fund I closed at $50,000,000 in January 2005 with Thiel as cofounder and GP -- that is 82.4% of the 2005 fund100 bar of $60,662,912, i.e. it misses by only 17.6%. Had the debut fund been $61M rather than $50M this row would date 2005, not 2007. The $50M figure is stated by both TechCrunch and Wikipedia, so the miss is on a firm number, but it is close and is recorded here deliberately. a6: 2014, Founders Fund V, "$1 billion" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founders_Fund) -- the first billion-dollar flagship, roughly 4.5x the hit fund.

name: Paul Thomas Anderson
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED, and independently of oscars.org, which the roster recorded as HTTP 403 and which was not retried. Wikipedia's 98th Academy Awards article (ceremony 15 March 2026) names him twice: Best Picture -- "One Battle After Another -- Adam Somner (posth.), Sara Murphy, and Paul Thomas Anderson, producers" -- and Best Director -- "Paul Thomas Anderson -- One Battle After Another" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/98th_Academy_Awards). a1: born 26 June 1970, Studio City, Los Angeles (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Thomas_Anderson). a2: 1988, high school graduation from Montclair College Preparatory School -- his LAST COMPLETED CREDENTIAL, per the dropout rule. He completed no tertiary credential: Wikipedia says he "spent two semesters as an English major at Emerson College" and left New York University after about two days of film school, and other accounts add an uncompleted stint at Santa Monica College. The year comes from two sourced facts rather than a stated graduation date: Emanuel Levy's Oscar-directors profile states "he wrote and filmed his first production as a senior in high school at Montclair Prep" and dates that film, The Dirk Diggler Story, to 1988 (https://emanuellevy.com/oscar/oscar-directors-anderson-paul-thomas-background-career-awards-filmography/); a US senior year ending in 1988 means a 1988 graduation. Conf medium because no source states the graduation year outright; the Montclair College Preparatory School Wikipedia page lists him as an alumnus with no year. a3: 1993, Cigarettes & Coffee -- "On a budget of $10,000 ... Anderson made Cigarettes & Coffee (1993), a short film" (Wikipedia). Short-film work is treated as a3 and the feature debut as a4, following p101 Jane Campion (a3 = shorts from 1982, a4 = feature debut 1989). Wikipedia also says he "began his career as a production assistant on television, films, music videos, and game shows", which would be an earlier a3, but gives no year for it and two attempts (Wikipedia, Emanuel Levy) produced none, so the dated short is used instead. a4: 1996, Hard Eight, his feature debut (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_Eight_(film)). SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK: not applicable in company form -- he is a writer-director with no earlier venture. The equivalent check, whether an earlier WORK crossed the audience bar first, was run and is recorded below. AUD1M PINNED 1997: Boogie Nights, released 10 October 1997. Wikipedia states "It eventually earned $26.4 million in the United States and $16.7 million in foreign markets for a worldwide box office total of $43.1 million" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boogie_Nights). The US average admission price in 1997 was about $4.59, so $26.4M domestic implies roughly 5.7 million paid admissions; even at an implausibly high $10 per ticket it would be 2.6 million. Margin over the 1M bar is roughly 470% on the domestic gross alone -- not close. Same theatrical-gross-implies-admissions logic as p101 Campion and p83 Zhao. NOTE THE CRITERION IS AUDIENCE, NOT MONEY: aud1m counts people, so the constant-dollar deflator cannot move this date, and no CPI conversion applies. EARLIER WORK RULED OUT WITH A FIGURE: his feature debut Hard Eight (1996) grossed $222,806 in total (Wikipedia infobox), which at 1996 ticket prices is roughly 47,000 admissions -- about 5% of the 1M bar, so it cannot be the hit. The only earlier works are the 1988 school-made short The Dirk Diggler Story and the 1993 short Cigarettes & Coffee, festival items with no audience claim. a6: 2026, Academy Awards for Best Director and Best Picture (as a producer) for One Battle After Another, ceremony 15 March 2026 -- twenty-nine years after the audience hit.

name: SZA
notes: LIST MEMBERSHIP CONFIRMED from the Recording Academy's own results page. Wikipedia states she graduated Columbia High School in 2008 and then attended Delaware State University as a marine biology major but dropped out during her final semester, so no degree was completed. a3: 14 July 2013, signed to Top Dawg Entertainment (Wikipedia) -- her first professional contract in music. a4: 29 October 2012, See.SZA.Run, her first self-released EP and first own venture, predating the label deal. SERIAL-FOUNDER CHECK: not applicable in company form. The equivalent check -- whether an earlier work of hers crossed the 1M audience bar -- was run: the self-released EPs See.SZA.Run (2012), S (2013) and Z (2014) carry no gold/platinum certification and no audience claim, so the debut album cycle is the first crossing among her own releases. OWN-WORK BOUNDARY, PER THE BATCH RULING, AND IT DEPARTS FROM p53. This row is dated from SZA's OWN SOLO OUTPUT ONLY. The 2026 Record Of The Year track "luther" is a Kendrick Lamar record on which she is a co-credited feature and is explicitly NOT used; Kendrick Lamar is already p52 in this study with hit entity "good kid, m.A.A.d city", and the hit_entity here (Ctrl) does not collide with it. Note that p53 Tems treated a FEATURED credit (Wizkid's "Essence" featuring Tems) as her own work; that precedent is deliberately not followed here on the batch ruling's instruction. IF IT WERE followed, her featured credit on ScHoolboy Q's "Studio" (2014, later RIAA platinum) could pull this row several years earlier -- flagged so the adversarial re-check sees the fork rather than rediscovering it. BOUNDED AUD1M 2017-2018, BOTH ENDS SOURCED, same shape as p84 Nguyen and p100 Whitehead. Lower end: Ctrl was released 9 June 2017 and its lead single "Love Galore" on 28 April 2017 (Wikipedia) -- a work cannot have an audience before it exists, which is the frame's founding-year lower bound applied to a release. Upper end: The FADER, 2 March 2018, read in full: "SZA's 2017 debut Ctrl has passed 1 million sales and is now certified platinum", with the certification "confirmed on March 1 by the R.I.A.A." (https://www.thefader.com/2018/03/02/sza-ctrl-platinum). Billboard ran the same story on the same date but its article URL 307-redirects to a paywall proxy that could not be read, so it is not used as the citation. RIAA Platinum = 1,000,000 units, the same instrument p53 Tems and p52 Kendrick were dated on. Midpoint used by the clocks is 2017.5. WHY NOT PINNED TO 2017: the single "Love Galore" reached RIAA Platinum before the album did -- HotNewHipHop reported "Ctrl" going gold and "Love Galore" going platinum in an article whose content places it in October 2017, which would pin 2017 -- but that page carries a 2022 modified date and states no certification date, and the RIAA gold-and-platinum database's search endpoint returned an empty body to curl, so no citable 2017 certification date was obtained after two attempts. The bound is therefore left at 2017-2018 rather than pinned on a page whose date cannot be trusted. NOTE THE CRITERION IS AUDIENCE, NOT MONEY: aud1m counts people, so the constant-2026-dollar deflator does not apply and no CPI conversion was made. a6: 2026, the 68th Annual Grammy Awards (ceremony 1 February 2026), where she won Record Of The Year and Best Melodic Rap Performance -- the award that put her on the roster, recorded as the scale marker rather than as the hit.
